environmentScrub: Every suite and rig command ran with this pane's LEGION_*/DISPATCH_*/JJ_* variables unset (scrubbed.sh / rig-up.sh); the worker-bin gh shim was removed from PATH for the rig.
observations: Later design-approved / design-changes-requested wakes were routed to the active phase worker (implementer), not the architect — pre-existing routeActive rule, also seen by the implementer.

Production profile `legion` holds pi-legion-envoy 1.17.0 (daemon API contract 1); this daemon refuses to boot against it by design, so the plugin from this commit must be installed there before the daemon deploys.

Under load ~200 the daemon logged 'failed to connect controller/architect shim socket on ready: negotiate_protocol timed out after 5000ms' for both panes in both rigs; sessions proceeded normally (worker_rpc_timeout_seconds default 5, pre-existing).
Live Dispatch events carry top-level `project` and `artifact_id: null` fields that the fixture envelopes omit; payload fields are identical.
The daemon writes <state_dir>/bin/legion and secrets/dispatch-token before verifyLegionPluginContract runs; state.json is not written.
POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/reviews rejects a body carrying `actor` with 400 unknown field (strict decode) — Dispatch API hygiene, not this change.

Confirmed by reading: dispatch-client.ts:108 now says `migrateV24State`'s resolver for a v24 design gate; legion-state.test.ts:880/:956/:963 say v24 (the remaining 'v23' at :791-794 is the locator migration's own fixture, correct).

scripts/smoke/up.sh hardcodes the NATS container name legion-smoke-nats, so two rigs on one box cannot coexist without editing the script (this run needed a copy); a SMOKE_NATS_NAME override or deriving the name from SMOKE_PROJECT would remove that.

At load ~170 the live-tmux daemon test 'probes a real tmux pane as alive…' needs 5.2-5.9 s and misses bun's 5 s default every time; it passes with a longer timeout. Consider a per-test timeout on the LEGION_TMUX_LIVE tests.
